title: Response Window Action Authorization Bypass in Combat
description: During active combat response windows (FLASH_1, BLOCK_DECLARATION, FLASH_2), turnControlledTypes authorization checks are gated behind if (!isWinActive), allowing unauthenticated or non-priority players to execute PLAY_CARD, SUMMON, SET_BURST, and USE_CORE while combat is in progress.
root_cause: SessionManager conditions turn-controlled action enforcement on !isWinActive without adding PLAY_CARD, SUMMON, SET_BURST, and USE_CORE to responseWindowActions or checking active player priority during active windows.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Submitting a SUMMON, PLAY_CARD, or USE_CORE action via submitPlayerAction while another player has priority in FLASH_1 or BLOCK_DECLARATION.
reproduction_steps: 1. Alice declares attack, opening FLASH_1 with Bob holding priority. 2. Alice immediately submits PLAY_CARD or SUMMON. 3. Action succeeds and executes onto field.
impact: Complete breakdown of combat step progression; unauthorized out-of-turn summoning and card casting during opponent response windows.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.2 & M.3 claimed strict action authority)
automated_test_status: REPRODUCED (No existing regression test prevented this)
proposed_remediation: Reorder authorization logic in session_manager.js so that during active response windows, all actions outside responseWindowActions and INTERACTION_RESPONSE are strictly rejected with RESPONSE_WINDOW_ACTIVE.
regression_risk: LOW (Protects engine turn and window progression)
verification_criteria: Submitting non-window actions during active response windows must fail with 403 / RESPONSE_WINDOW_ACTIVE regardless of caller.

title: Combat Lifecycle Response Window Premature Closure & Flash 2 Bypass
description: Direct calls to game.declareBlock() and game.resolveDirectHit() close active response windows and set combat stage directly to BP_COMPARE or END without proper window lifecycle transitions, completely skipping Flash 2 and defender interaction.
root_cause: engine/index.js contains legacy direct combat transition code that closes active windows and overrides stage rather than driving through TimingWindowManager.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Calling game.declareBlock() or game.resolveDirectHit() directly on the engine instance.
reproduction_steps: 1. Initiate combat. 2. Call game.declareBlock(blockerId). 3. Notice stage becomes BP_COMPARE and window is closed without opening FLASH_2.
impact: Flash 2 is completely bypassed during programmatic or direct block declarations; defensive cards cannot be played after block declaration.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.3 claimed mandatory Flash 2 timing)
proposed_remediation: Route all combat state transitions through TimingWindowManager.handleBlockDeclaration() and open FLASH_2 before BP comparison.
regression_risk: MEDIUM (Requires updating tests that call declareBlock directly during FLASH_1)
verification_criteria: Declaring a block must always transition combat stage to FLASH_2 and grant Defender priority 1 before BP comparison.

title: Candidate Generation Divergence from Validation Rules
description: ResponseWindowManager.calculateFlashCandidates duplicates timing checks using an ad-hoc English regex instead of calling flash_timing.js:validateFlashTiming(). Japanese-script cards restricted to opponent attack step are offered as legal candidates to the attacking player, but subsequently rejected upon execution.
root_cause: Failure to use the single source of truth (validateFlashTiming) in candidate generation.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Player inspecting legalResponseCandidates during FLASH_1 sees cards that cannot be legally played.
reproduction_steps: 1. Give attacker a card with effect "フラッシュ (相手のアタックステップ)". 2. Inspect candidates in FLASH_1; card is offered. 3. Submitting card fails with OPPONENT_ATTACK_STEP_ONLY.
impact: Desynchronization between UI candidate offering and engine execution validation; player confusion and rejected action errors.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.3.1 claimed unified Flash candidate generation)
proposed_remediation: Replace calculateFlashCandidates ad-hoc logic with calls to validateFlashTiming().
regression_risk: LOW (Ensures candidate generation strictly matches validation rules)
verification_criteria: All candidates returned by calculateFlashCandidates must pass validateFlashTiming without exception.

title: Direct Engine Public API Surface Bypasses Participant Authority
description: Public methods on game (declareAttack, declareBlock, resolveDirectHit, playCard, advanceStep) perform zero caller authorization checks. Authority is enforced solely at the SessionManager boundary. Any direct internal caller, test, or engine consumer completely bypasses participant identity and turn authority.
root_cause: Engine core was originally designed for single-process local play; multi-tenant authority was layered externally in SessionManager rather than inside the engine boundary.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Direct invocation of game.* methods in integration tests or internal scripts.
reproduction_steps: 1. Call game.declareAttack(stackId, "opponent") during player turn. 2. Attack succeeds without validating caller authorization.
impact: Lack of defense-in-depth; potential for server components or plugins to trigger state changes bypassing session locks.
historical_claim_status: PARTIALLY VERIFIED (Enforced in SessionManager, absent in engine core)
proposed_remediation: Accept optional authContext in engine core methods or validate authenticated player identity against game.state.activePlayer.
verification_criteria: Engine core methods must reject actions when caller is not the authorized participant.

title: PromptManager Validation Error Reason Discarded
description: In submitInteractionResponse(), when usePromptManager is true, promptManager.resolve() returns a boolean, discarding result.reason and result.code from interactionController.respond().
root_cause: submitInteractionResponse returns { success: Boolean(res), interactionId } without preserving detailed error reasons.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Submitting an invalid interaction response in PromptManager mode.
reproduction_steps: 1. Submit invalid interaction response with usePromptManager: true. 2. Result lacks failure reason.
impact: Clients receive generic false without explanation for why an interaction was rejected.
historical_claim_status: PARTIALLY VERIFIED
proposed_remediation: Preserve promptManager resolution details and error reasons in return object.
verification_criteria: submitInteractionResponse must return detailed error codes on failure.

title: Arbitrary Unit Injection and Core Minting via SUMMON Action
description: Any authenticated player can submit an action of type SUMMON with arbitrary card payload and core count. SessionManager directly instantiates the card onto the field refreshed and mints cores out of nowhere, completely bypassing hand zone checks, cost payment, and core conservation laws.
root_cause: SUMMON action branch in session_manager.js directly constructs a new card instance from client-supplied JSON and pushes it to p.field with client-specified cores.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Client sending { type: "SUMMON", card: { name: "Hacked", bp: 999999 }, cores: 100 } over WebSocket or HTTP.
reproduction_steps: 1. Connect to match. 2. Submit action { type: "SUMMON", card: { name: "Cheat" }, cores: 50 }. 3. Unit is spawned on field with 50 newly minted cores.
impact: Catastrophic game integrity failure; arbitrary card creation and unlimited core generation in persistent multiplayer matches.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.2 claimed strict action validation)
proposed_remediation: Remove the client-facing SUMMON action type or restrict it exclusively to internal engine effect resolution; player summons must use PLAY_CARD referencing existing cards in hand.
verification_criteria: External SUMMON actions must be rejected; card summons must strictly originate from hand and consume reserve cores.

title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary Forward Proxy / Server-Side Request Forgery
description: Endpoint /api/proxy-image?url=... is an unauthenticated open forward proxy without domain allowlists, private IP filtering, or port restrictions. Any external caller can trigger requests to localhost, internal network services, and cloud metadata endpoints.
root_cause: HTTP client blindly fetches targetUrl without validating protocol, hostname, or IP address against an allowlist.
attack_vector_or_trigger: HTTP GET /api/proxy-image?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or http://localhost:8080/internal.
reproduction_steps: 1. Send GET request to /api/proxy-image?url=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/sessions/health. 2. Server proxies the response.
impact: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF); internal port scanning, access to cloud metadata, and internal network reconnaissance.
historical_claim_status: UNVERIFIED (Never audited in previous phases)
proposed_remediation: Enforce strict domain allowlist (e.g. battle-spirits.fandom.com, official bandai domains) and reject private/loopback/link-local IP addresses.
regression_risk: LOW (Only legitimate card artwork domains need to be proxied)
verification_criteria: Requests to localhost, private IPs, or non-whitelisted domains must return 403 Forbidden.

title: Sensitive File and Database Disclosure via Web Root Static Handler
description: Static file handler in server.js serves files from __dirname without blocking sensitive file extensions, dotfiles, or database files. Unauthenticated callers can directly download battle_spirits.db (45MB database containing session tokens and player states) and .git/config.
root_cause: No blacklist or whitelist for served file extensions; dotfiles and database files are served as application/octet-stream.
attack_vector_or_trigger: HTTP GET /battle_spirits.db or HTTP GET /.git/config.
reproduction_steps: 1. Send GET request to http://localhost:3000/battle_spirits.db. 2. Server streams the complete 45MB SQLite database.
impact: Complete exposure of all active matches, player authentication tokens, session history, and version control metadata.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.2 claimed full credential isolation)
proposed_remediation: Restrict static file serving strictly to a dedicated public/ or ui/ directory, or explicitly reject requests for .db, .git, .env, and hidden dotfiles.
verification_criteria: Requests for battle_spirits.db, .git, or files outside public assets must return 404/403.

title: Complete Response Window Loss Upon Session Restoration / Reconnect
description: ResponseWindowManager initializes this.windowStack = [] in its constructor and never re-populates it from restoredState.responseWindow. Restoring a match from SQLite (or reconnecting after memory eviction) wipes active combat windows, soft-locking the match in COMBAT_ALREADY_IN_PROGRESS while passPriority fails with NO_ACTIVE_RESPONSE_WINDOW.
root_cause: ResponseWindowManager lacks state rehydration logic to reconstruct windowStack from deserialized state.responseWindow.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Server restart or match reload from database while FLASH_1, BLOCK_DECLARATION, or FLASH_2 is active.
reproduction_steps: 1. Declare attack opening FLASH_1. 2. Save snapshot and clear memory cache. 3. Call restoreMatch(). 4. getCurrentWindow() returns null; combat is deadlocked.
impact: Any reconnection during combat breaks response window progression and permanently freezes the match.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.1 & M.3 claimed seamless reconnection during active windows)
proposed_remediation: In ResponseWindowManager constructor or game initialization, inspect game.state.responseWindow and push it onto this.windowStack if status is OPEN or SUSPENDED.
verification_criteria: Restored matches must preserve getCurrentWindow(), windowType, and priority player exactly as before serialization.

title: WebSocket Single-Use Transport Ticket Action Submission Failure
description: When a client connects over WebSocket using a single-use transport ticket (ticketParam), authToken is undefined. Subsequent WebSocket heartbeats and action submissions fail with AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED because submitPlayerAction requires authToken.
root_cause: WebSocket connection handler redeems ticket to determine viewerSide, but does not associate or pass the ticket credentials to submitPlayerAction or recordHeartbeat.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Client connecting via short-lived ticket and attempting to submit actions over WS.
reproduction_steps: 1. Issue transport ticket. 2. Connect WS with ?ticket=... 3. Send action message. 4. WS returns AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED error.
impact: Transport ticket flow cannot be used for bidirectional WebSocket gameplay; clients are forced to pass raw auth tokens in connection URLs.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.2 claimed ticket-based WS connectivity)
proposed_remediation: Store authenticated playerId and session credentials on the WebSocket connection context and pass them to submitPlayerAction.
verification_criteria: WebSocket clients authenticated via transport tickets must be able to submit actions and heartbeats without raw auth tokens.

title: BLOCK_DECLARATION Window Rejection of game.passPriority
description: BLOCK_DECLARATION response window only registers DECLARE_BLOCK and PASS_BLOCK as legal actions. game.passPriority() hardcodes { action: "PASS" }, which is rejected with ACTION_NOT_ELIGIBLE_IN_WINDOW. The engine provides no passBlock() or declineBlock() public method.
root_cause: Mismatch between game.passPriority action payload and BLOCK_DECLARATION legal action definitions.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Calling game.passPriority() during BLOCK_DECLARATION window.
reproduction_steps: 1. Advance combat past Flash 1 to BLOCK_DECLARATION. 2. Call game.passPriority("opponent"). 3. Action rejected with ACTION_NOT_ELIGIBLE_IN_WINDOW.
impact: Defending player cannot decline block via standard passPriority API; combat becomes stuck unless client submits undocumented PASS_BLOCK payload.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.3 claimed unified passPriority handling across all windows)
proposed_remediation: Update game.passPriority to map to PASS_BLOCK when the active window is BLOCK_DECLARATION, or add PASS to BLOCK_DECLARATION eligible actions.
verification_criteria: Calling game.passPriority during BLOCK_DECLARATION must cleanly decline block and transition to direct hit / Flash 2.

title: Unconditional Flash 2 Step Skip on No-Block
description: In handlePassBlock(), declining to block unconditionally calls resolveDirectHit(), skipping Flash 2 entirely. Official Battle Spirits rules grant both players Flash Timing 2 after block declaration regardless of whether a block was declared.
root_cause: Hardcoded direct hit execution in handlePassBlock() with comment "SKIPS FLASH 2! Proceeds directly to Direct Hit!".
attack_vector_or_trigger: Defender declines block; attacker or defender cannot activate combat-ending or damage-modifying Flash magic in Flash 2.
reproduction_steps: 1. Defender passes block. 2. Direct hit resolves immediately without opening FLASH_2.
impact: Rule deviation from official Battle Spirits rules; players denied opportunity to respond before life reduction.
historical_claim_status: PARTIALLY VERIFIED (Implemented by design but violates official rules format)
proposed_remediation: Open FLASH_2 window after PASS_BLOCK and resolve direct hit only after FLASH_2 closes.
regression_risk: MEDIUM (Changes combat window sequence for unblocked attacks)
verification_criteria: Declining block must transition to FLASH_2 before resolving direct hit.

title: 265 of 364 Registered Runtime Keywords Are Inactive Stubs
file_paths: engine/keywords/wave1.js; engine/keywords/wave2.js; engine/keywords/wave3.js; engine/keywords/wave4.js; engine/keywords/wave5.js; engine/keywords/wave6.js
description: Out of 364 registered runtime keywords, 265 (72.8%) possess completely empty hooks objects (hooks: {}). Only 99 keywords have any registered lifecycle hooks.
root_cause: Mass generation of keyword stub definitions to satisfy registry count metrics without implementing lifecycle mechanics.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Cards possessing any of these 265 keywords triggering in battle.
reproduction_steps: 1. Register all keywords. 2. Filter registry entries with Object.keys(k.hooks).length === 0. 3. Count is 265.
impact: Keywords appear in registry and card text but do nothing during gameplay.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase W.1 & W.2 claimed 364 implemented runtime keywords)
proposed_remediation: Implement real lifecycle hooks or classify unhooked keywords as Stubs / Unimplemented.
verification_criteria: Keyword support matrix must accurately reflect 265 keywords as lacking active hooks.

title: 110 Keywords Completely Lack Executable Code
description: 110 keywords in the runtime registry have neither hooks nor any executable methods. They are pure data objects containing only id, name, and wave properties.
root_cause: Placeholder registration of keywords without executable implementation.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Attempting to resolve or query mechanics for any of the 110 stub keywords.
reproduction_steps: 1. Inspect all keyword objects in registry. 2. 110 objects contain zero functions.
impact: False claims of keyword implementation; 110 keywords are purely declarative placeholders.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED
proposed_remediation: Document 110 keywords as Data-Only Stubs in support matrix.
verification_criteria: Report accurately separates executable keywords from data-only placeholders.

title: 40 Keyword Custom Methods Disconnected and Orphaned from Engine Flow
description: 40 out of 46 custom methods defined on keywords (executeWhirlwind, executeTrueAwaken, executeSoulDrive, executeUTrigger, executeBunshin, executeSeal, etc.) are never invoked anywhere in engine/index.js, flow.js, or resolver.js. They exist solely to be called by isolated synthetic unit tests.
root_cause: Methods were implemented on keyword objects but never wired into the engine's ability resolution pipeline or timing windows.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Playing real cards with Whirlwind, Soul Drive, U-Trigger, or Bunshin in an actual game.
reproduction_steps: 1. Grep entire engine/ directory for calls to executeWhirlwind or executeSoulDrive. 2. Zero callers found outside tests.
impact: Orphaned implementations: tests pass because tests call the functions directly, but in an actual match the cards do nothing.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase W.2 claimed verified runtime mechanics)
proposed_remediation: Wire keyword execution methods into resolver.js and TimingWindowManager so abilities invoke them during real gameplay.
verification_criteria: Playing a card with Soul Drive or Whirlwind during an actual match must execute the keyword method.

title: Game Keywords Registry Object Disconnected from Engine Execution
description: game.keywords is instantiated at game creation (line 316) and attached to game (line 340), but is never referenced anywhere in engine/. Keywords like Clash, Curse, and Burst are resolved via hardcoded ad-hoc branches in engine/index.js rather than the registry.
root_cause: Ad-hoc keyword handling was added directly into combat flow instead of querying game.keywords.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Modifying keyword definitions in registry has zero effect on engine behavior.
reproduction_steps: 1. Grep engine/ for game.keywords. 2. Zero usages found.
impact: Architectural fragmentation; keyword registry is largely a parallel data structure ignored by the core engine.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED
proposed_remediation: Refactor engine/index.js combat hooks to query game.keywords dynamically.
verification_criteria: Combat flow must query game.keywords rather than hardcoded string checks.

title: Failing Keyword Unit Tests on Main Branch
description: 4 tests in tests/keyword_registry.test.js (Windstorm, Ultra Holy Life, True-Curse, Fierce Windstorm) and 1 test in tests/keywords_waves4_5_6.test.js (Ultra Awaken) currently fail on main when executed with node --test.
root_cause: Tests were written assuming synchronous block declarations without response windows, but subsequent changes added FLASH_TIMING_NOT_CLOSED guards, causing declareBlock() calls in tests to fail silently.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Running node --test tests/keyword_registry.test.js.
reproduction_steps: 1. Run node --test tests/keyword_registry.test.js. 2. Observe 4 test failures.
impact: Core regression suite has broken tests on main; keyword mechanics verification is compromised.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Claimed 57/57 dedicated keyword tests passing)
proposed_remediation: Update test cases to pass priority before declaring block or update declareBlock to handle test window progression.
verification_criteria: All tests in keyword_registry.test.js and keywords_waves4_5_6.test.js must pass cleanly.

title: Master Verification Runner Omits 71.6% of Test Corpus
description: scripts/run_master_verification.mjs executes only 74 out of 261 test files in tests/ (omitting 187 test suites and over 1,100 test cases). Running this script leaves nearly three quarters of the project untested.
root_cause: Runner hardcodes a curated list of suites and excludes the vast majority of domain tests.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Relying on master runner as evidence of complete project health.
reproduction_steps: 1. Compare suites in run_master_verification.mjs (74) against fs.readdirSync("tests") (261). 2. 187 files omitted.
impact: False sense of project verification; regressions in the 187 omitted test files go completely undetected.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Claimed comprehensive test coverage)
proposed_remediation: Expand runner to discover and run all test files using an isolated database environment.
verification_criteria: Master verification must cover all 261 test files.

title: Master Runner Overwrites Historical Report Directories
description: scripts/run_master_verification.mjs defines OUT_DIRS containing historical phase directories (reports/phase_m3_response_windows, reports/phase_m1, reports/phase4d) and writes results into them, destroying historical audit records.
root_cause: Runner was designed to update multiple legacy report folders simultaneously.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Executing node scripts/run_master_verification.mjs.
reproduction_steps: 1. Inspect OUT_DIRS in script. 2. Observe paths to past phase report folders.
impact: Violation of audit immutability and report preservation.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED
proposed_remediation: Restrict runner outputs to a dedicated reports/latest/ or phase-specific directory.
verification_criteria: Running test runners must never modify historical report directories.

title: DefaultPromptResolver Silently Auto-Decides Critical Combat Choices
description: Games initialized without interactive: true or automatedProvider fall back to DefaultPromptResolver, which automatically selects accepted: true, triggers bursts, passes Flash, and declines blocks without player agency.
root_cause: DefaultPromptResolver provides artificial automatic choices to allow headless unit tests to run without interaction handlers.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Running matches without explicit interactive: true flag.
reproduction_steps: 1. createGame() without interactive: true. 2. Observe all prompts resolve automatically without pausing.
impact: Tests pass automatically because engine makes choices on behalf of players; hides missing player prompt handling.
historical_claim_status: PARTIALLY VERIFIED
proposed_remediation: Require explicit interactive mode or mock interaction controller for all test executions.
verification_criteria: All interactive choices must require explicit interaction resolution.

title: Failed PLAY_CARD Actions Committing to Database Ledger
description: When game.playCard() fails and returns { success: false, reason: ... }, session_manager.js marks actionResult = { success: true, played: cardId, result: res }, committing the failed action to the database transaction and ledger.
root_cause: PLAY_CARD execution block wraps the return value in success: true without checking res.success.
attack_vector_or_trigger: Player submitting PLAY_CARD with insufficient cores.
reproduction_steps: 1. Submit PLAY_CARD without enough cores. 2. actionResult is recorded as success: true in event ledger.
impact: Event ledger and database record failed card plays as successful actions, corrupting audit history.
historical_claim_status: CONTRADICTED (Phase M.2 claimed failed actions are never committed)
proposed_remediation: Check res.success and throw an error if false, triggering in-memory rollback and preventing commit.
verification_criteria: Failed card plays must throw an error and never be recorded as successful in the ledger.
